channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbek President Participates in Uzbek-Korean Business Forum
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev and South Korean Prime Minister Han Duck-soo attended the opening of a joint business forum. Over 300 representatives from state structures and businesses participated. The forum aimed to enhance trade, investment, and joint projects, leveraging Uzbekistan's resources and Korea's technology.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Mining Sector Potential Presented to British Businesses
item.description: British companies were informed about Kyrgyzstan's investment climate and recent changes in its mining sector during a meeting organized by the UK Embassy in Bishkek. Representatives discussed geological exploration, mineral processing, environmental safety, and critical mineral development programs.

item.title: Sadyr Japarov Arrives in South Korea for Official Visit
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov has arrived in South Korea for an official visit, where he will hold bilateral meetings with top Korean leadership. He will also participate in the first Central Asia-Republic of Korea summit and a special session of the business summit.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan, Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan may simplify travel within Turkic states using ID cards
item.description: Citizens of five Turkic states may soon travel within the Organization of Turkic States (OTS) using only ID cards, without a foreign passport. Kyrgyzstan, Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Azerbaijan, and Turkey are included in the proposal, aiming to expand the current agreement between Azerbaijan and Turkey. The OTS Secretary-General confirmed the initiative is being actively prepared.

item.title: Tajikistan seeks investment for new solar power plant construction
item.description: Tajikistan is seeking investment for the construction of new solar power plants. The country has discussed potential investment in this sector with the Chinese company "LONGi". Further details on the investment plans and the specific projects are expected.

item.title: Uzbekistan proposes reduced working hours for older employees
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to introduce reduced working hours for women over 55 and men over 60 starting January 1, 2027, with average wages maintained. This measure is part of a draft presidential decree on pension system reform. The proposal also includes changes for self-employed individuals and cancellation of social tax benefits.

item.title: Tashkent Hosts International Business Forum for Regional Dialogue
item.description: Tashkent served as a venue for an international business forum within the "International Leadership Awards" project. Entrepreneurs and business representatives from Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, Azerbaijan, Turkey, France, and Kyrgyzstan participated. They shared experiences, discussed new ideas, and identified cooperation prospects across various sectors including energy and tourism.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Considers Limiting Night Access for Children in Anti-Cafes and Anti-Cinemas
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is considering a bill to restrict children's nighttime access to anti-cafes and anti-cinemas without parental supervision. The Ministry of Labor proposes the measure due to risks of delinquency and exploitation. The bill aims to address establishments operating late hours with private rooms, which are not covered by current regulations.

item.title: Uzbekistan Plans Pension System Reforms and Increased State Contributions by 2027
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to reform its pension calculation method and expand the funded pension system starting January 1, 2027. The proposal includes extending the income calculation period for pensions and excluding 10% of the lowest earnings. Higher income earners will see an increased ceiling for pension calculations from April 2028.

item.title: Tajikistan and South Korea Sign Industrial and Technology Cooperation Agreements
item.description: During the first 'C5+1' ministerial meeting in Seoul, Tajikistan and South Korea signed memorandums of understanding on industrial and supply chain cooperation. The agreements aim to develop industrial infrastructure, boost trade and investment, and foster collaboration in critical minerals, AI, and smart manufacturing.

item.title: Uzbek President Meets South Korean Prime Minister in Seoul
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with South Korean Prime Minister Han Duck-soo in Seoul. They discussed strengthening strategic partnerships in trade, economy, investment, technology, and transport. Special attention was given to innovation, digital economy, cybersecurity, and critical mineral processing.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Launches 'One Health' Project Amid Regional Conference
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has officially launched its component of the 'One Health' initiative during a regional conference in Bishkek. Government representatives, the World Bank, and international organizations discussed integrated risks, including infections, antimicrobial resistance, and climate change, highlighting biosecurity investments' economic benefits.

item.title: Germany Interested in Long-Term Cooperation with Uzbekistan
item.description: German Bundestag deputies met with Sodik Safoyev, First Deputy Chairman of the Senate of Uzbekistan's Oliy Majlis. They discussed bilateral relations, inter-parliamentary dialogue, and expanding cooperation in science and education. Germany expressed interest in long-term partnership with Uzbekistan, recognizing its economic potential and human capital.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan completes construction and renovation of 81 schools for new academic year
item.description: Construction and major renovations of 81 schools in Kyrgyzstan were finished before the 2026–2027 academic year, according to the Ministry of Construction. Of these, 40 schools were built new, and 41 underwent major renovations. The Jalal-Abad region saw the most projects with 26 schools. An additional 36 schools are being prepared for commissioning.

item.title: Central Asia WHO official discusses 'One Health' concept and zoonotic threats
item.description: Merekke Taituabayev, head of the World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH) sub-regional representation for Central Asia, discussed the 'One Health' concept, which links humans, animals, and the environment. He stated that approximately 70 percent of human infectious diseases are zoonotic, originating from animals. Taituabayev emphasized the need for better preparedness for future pandemics, citing COVID-19 as an example.

item.title: Uzbekistan to gradually liberalize liquefied gas market
item.description: Uzbekistan will gradually liberalize its liquefied gas market, according to a presidential decree signed by Shavkat Mirziyoyev. The reforms aim to ensure stable supply, efficient resource use, attract private investment, and transition to targeted social support. A new company, LPG-Trade, will be established under Hududgazta'minot to manage supply and ensure financial transparency.

item.title: Chingiz Akhmatov appointed First Deputy Prosecutor General of Kyrgyzstan
item.description: Chingiz Akhmatov has been appointed First Deputy Prosecutor General of Kyrgyzstan. Prosecutor General Melis Bekturganov introduced Akhmatov to the staff, highlighting his professional experience. Akhmatov expressed gratitude for the confidence and pledged to strengthen the rule of law. He becomes the fifth deputy to the Prosecutor General.

item.title: Uzbekistan proposes raising retirement age to 63 for men, 58 for women by 2039
item.description: Uzbekistan is proposing to gradually increase the retirement age to 63 for men and 58 for women by 2039. A draft presidential decree also suggests changes to pension calculation methods, including extending the period for considering work experience and excluding lower-income periods. Incentives for continuing work past retirement age are also proposed.

item.title: Tajikistan Invites Foreign Investment for Digital Economy Development
item.description: Tajikistan's State Committee on Investments presented a roadmap for developing its digital economy, artificial intelligence, and innovations. Priority sectors for capital include energy, industry, transport, agriculture, tourism, and finance, with a strong focus on ICT. The period from 2025-2030 is designated as the Years of Digital Economy and Innovation Development.

item.title: Astana to Host Major International Festival Featuring AI-Generated Films
item.description: Astana will host the 'Astana AI Film Festival' (AAIFF-2026) in October, showcasing over 8,000 films from 125 countries. The festival received 8,067 submissions, with many participants experimenting with AI in filmmaking. Organizers note the rapid development of AI cinema, highlighting Astana as a hub for this new direction.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Partially Cover Diesel Costs for Agricultural Enterprises
item.description: Uzbekistan will temporarily subsidize a portion of diesel fuel costs for agricultural enterprises purchasing through commodity exchanges. The compensation applies to fuel bought between July 1 and December 1, 2026, if the exchange price exceeds 15 million UZS per ton, with a subsidy limit of 2 million UZS per ton.

item.title: Uzbekistan and South Korea Sign Key Agreements Ahead of Summit
item.description: Uzbekistan and South Korea signed important agreements in Seoul during a meeting focused on future cooperation in growth and innovation. The event, held before the first Central Asia-Republic of Korea summit, included ministers from Uzbekistan, South Korea, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, and Turkmenistan.

item.title: Uzbek President Holds Meetings with South Korean Companies on Investment Projects
item.description: Uzbekistan's President met with representatives of South Korean companies to discuss projects worth $8 billion. Discussions included developing the hotel business, producing electric and hybrid vehicles, supplying high-speed trains, and processing important minerals.

item.title: Tajik and Swiss scientists confirm permafrost presence on Hargush Pass
item.description: Scientists from Tajikistan's National Academy of Sciences and Fribourg University conducted geophysical research on Hargush Pass in Gorno-Badakhshan. The expedition aimed to identify and map permafrost layers. The findings confirm the existence of permafrost and perennial ice sheets, crucial for assessing climate change impacts and establishing long-term monitoring.

item.title: Tajikistan and EBRD sign memorandum for strategic investment in energy, transport, and education until 2030
item.description: Tajikistan's Finance Minister and the EBRD President signed a Memorandum of Understanding in London, establishing a strategic investment roadmap for 2026-2030. The partnership focuses on sustainable energy, irrigation modernization, economic governance, attracting private investment, transport development, and new educational facilities.

item.title: Uzbekistan and South Korea finalize $12 billion investment portfolio
item.description: Uzbekistan and South Korea have established a new investment portfolio totaling approximately $12 billion. This includes joint projects in sectors like healthcare, industry, IT, agriculture, energy, infrastructure, and education. The leaders also discussed creating a technological alliance and noted growth in trade and investment.

item.title: One-month military service cost increases in Uzbekistan
item.description: The cost of one month of military service in Uzbekistan has increased. The payment amount is tied to the minimum wage and has doubled in the last six years. Those joining the military can pay the fee in a lump sum or in installments over one year.

item.title: New Kia Model Production to Begin in Jizzakh, Uzbekistan
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev attended the launch ceremony for joint projects with leading South Korean companies and financial institutions in Jizzakh. Production of a new Kia model is set to commence in the region, signaling a significant step in automotive manufacturing collaboration.

item.title: Uzbekistan and South Korea May Establish Industrial-Technological Alliance
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev and South Korean Prime Minister Han Duck-soo opened a joint business forum. Over 300 representatives from government and business circles attended, including leaders from major Korean companies like Lotte Chemical and Hyundai Motor Group. The forum highlighted opportunities for increased trade and investment.

item.title: Uzbekneftgaz Prepares for Winter Season, Focuses on Gas Production and Supply
item.description: Uzbekneftgaz has begun a 30-day preparation phase for the autumn-winter season, focusing on gas extraction, well conditions, and stable supply. Despite significant efforts, some indicators remain below expectations. The company emphasizes the need for direct action at fields and wells to ensure gas availability for the public.

item.title: Chyngyz Akhmatov Appointed First Deputy Prosecutor General of Kyrgyzstan
item.description: Chyngyz Akhmatov has been appointed First Deputy Prosecutor General of Kyrgyzstan. He was introduced to the staff today. Akhmatov has worked in the prosecutor's office since 2004 and previously served as the Prosecutor of Osh region until his recent appointment.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Completes Construction and Renovation of 81 Schools for New Academic Year
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has completed the construction and renovation of 81 schools by the 2026-2027 academic year, according to the Ministry of Construction. Forty schools were built from scratch, and 41 underwent major renovations. Additional schools are nearing completion across various regions.

item.title: NABU to Assist Kyrgyzstan in Updating Red Book of Endangered Species
item.description: The German Nature and Biodiversity Conservation Union (NABU) will help Kyrgyzstan update its Red Book of Endangered Species. The project, funded with 21 million soms over 24 months, will use modern scientific data to assess rare species populations and threats.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Competition Committee Investigates WB Taxi Over Passenger Complaints
item.description: Uzbekistan's Committee for the Development of Competition and Protection of Consumer Rights has sent an inquiry to WB Taxi due to numerous passenger complaints. The committee noted an increase in complaints regarding taxi services, with nearly 20 related to WB Taxi reported between January and August. Issues include cars not arriving and lack of operator response.

item.title: One Kilogram of Psychotropic Substance Seized from Child's Electric Car in Bishkek
item.description: Kyrgyzstan authorities, with Russian cooperation, have intercepted a supply of psychotropic substances from Russia to Bishkek. A 20-year-old suspect was detained in Bishkek with a one-kilogram briquette of Alpha-PVP found in a child's electric car. The operation prevented the distribution of over 4,200 doses, with potential proceeds exceeding 4.5 million soms.

item.title: Turkic states' muftis adopt fatwa on artificial intelligence use
item.description: The 7th Meeting of the Council of Heads of Muslim Religious Boards of the Organization of Turkic States (OTS) in Baku resulted in the adoption of six fatwas, including one on the use of artificial intelligence in issuing religious rulings. Joint statements were also signed on family protection, Islam's stance on science and technology, and takfir.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Faces Potential Gasoline Shortages Due to Russian Supply Issues
item.description: Kyrgyzstan, heavily reliant on Russian gasoline imports, may face shortages. Russia is the primary supplier from the EAEU, accounting for 99% of Kyrgyzstan's imports in early 2026. Potential reductions or irregular supplies from Russia, due to domestic issues and export bans, could impact Kyrgyzstan's fuel availability despite EAEU exemptions.

item.title: Uzbek President Meets with Speaker of South Korean National Assembly
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with Speaker of the South Korean National Assembly Cho Jung-sik during a state visit. They emphasized the role of parliaments in advancing the strategic partnership, noting active inter-parliamentary groups and exchanges. Discussions also covered enhancing economic, investment, and cultural ties, and establishing parliamentary monitoring mechanisms.

item.title: CSTO Considers Resuming Cooperation with OSCE, Open to Dialogue with NATO
item.description: The CSTO sees value in resuming cooperation with the OSCE, with Secretary General Taalatbek Masadykov meeting his OSCE counterpart. The organization also remains open to dialogue with NATO, despite previous unsuccessful attempts. The CSTO prioritizes cooperation with traditional partners like the UN and SCO, while developing relations with new blocs.

item.title: Russian Drone Attack on Kyiv and Regions Kills One, Wounds Several
item.description: On September 15, 2026, Russian drones struck gas stations and warehouses in Kyiv, resulting in seven injuries, one of whom later died. Attacks also hit civilian infrastructure in Odesa region. Ukraine's air defense reportedly shot down 187 of 200 drones used.
